2.why: what follows is an appositive fragment; semicolon and period leave a fragment, no punctuation runs on; dash sets it off

3.why: comma splice; appositive noun phrase with relative clause fixes it; 'that' after comma and no-comma are wrong

4.why: so + adverb + that is idiomatic; 'slow' is adjective modifying verb; too/as do not pair with 'that'

5.why: no parallel action visible to justify 'Similarly'; turning the key off and retrying reads as an alternative to something the narrator did, so 'Instead'

6.why: opening dash after residents must be closed by a matching dash

7.why: comma splice; period separates two independent clauses; 'so' gives wrong logic

8.why: only choice showing an unpolished singer; D contradicts, B shows experience

9.why: run-on; 'when he was' subordinate clause after comma; semicolon before dependent clause wrong; comma alone splices

10.why: subject is singular 'nearly every plant'; present tense matches 'flowers roughly once' and 'it grows'

11.why: whom is object of 'calls' (she calls him the best voicer); which/that wrong for a person in nonrestrictive clause

12.why: 'Each one a sac' has no verb so it must attach as an absolute phrase after a comma; semicolon/period leave fragment; 'is' creates splice
